sections.title: Consonants: a-series
sections.note: On their own they are read with â [ɑː].

sections.title: Consonants: o-series
sections.note: On their own they are read with ô [ɔː].

sections.title: Vowel signs
sections.note: Each reads two ways, depending on the series of the consonant.

sections.title: Subscripts
sections.note: Consonant clusters: the second letter is written under the first.

groups.title: ក ខ ច ឆ
groups.tip: These are a-series consonants: on their own they are read with â [ɑː]. ក is kâ, ខ is khâ.

groups.title: ដ ត ថ ប
groups.tip: ដ dâ and ត tâ look alike: ដ has a curl at the top.

groups.title: ផ ស ហ អ
groups.tip: អ is a glottal stop. Vowels that start a word are written on it.

groups.title: ឋ ណ ឡ
groups.tip: Rarer a-series letters, mostly in borrowed words.

groups.title: គ ឃ ង ជ
groups.tip: o-series consonants are read with ô [ɔː]. គ kô sounds like ក kâ but with the o-series vowel.

groups.title: ឈ ញ ទ ធ
ន ព ភ ម
យ រ ល វ
ឌ ឍ
groups.tip: Two rare o-series letters, mostly in Pali and Sanskrit words.
A vowel sign reads one way after an a-series consonant and another after an o-series one.
Some vowel signs are written before the consonant, but they are still read after it.
The small circle ំ adds a final m.
The two small circles ះ add a final h.
Marks written above a letter change its sound.

groups.title: ឥ ឦ ឧ ឪ
groups.tip: Independent vowels stand alone, without a consonant. A few are common: ឥឡូវ "now", ឪពុក "father".
